items.text: Joe Wilson, a Republican member of the US House of Representatives, called the Houthis proxies of Iran and said no new terrorist colony would be allowed on the coast of the Gulf of Aden. He referred to the draft "Liberation of Yemen from Iran," which supports the Yemeni people and includes new sanctions. He also compared the Houthis to Bashar al-Assad and called for Yemen to be freed from Iran.

The Iran Human Rights Organization announced that at least 100 detainees from the January 2026 protests face the risk of execution. Among them are five women and five individuals under 18 years old. Additionally, 31 protesters have been executed since March 18.

Fars News Agency reported a drone attack by the US on two fishing boats near Bandar Kangan. Several fishermen went missing in the attack. Rescue and search operations are underway to locate the missing individuals.

Benjamin Netanyahu criticized the documentary "Naza" about military targeting in Gaza as part of a wave of provocations against Jews. Eyal Zamir ordered a review of possible legal actions regarding the documentary. Over 200 Israeli filmmakers supported the creators and called for protection of freedom of expression.

The minimum wage for workers and retirees has remained fixed recently, but living costs, especially food, have increased unprecedentedly. The point-to-point inflation of food items in August was estimated at about 130 percent. By the end of July, the cost of the food basket was about 10 million tomans higher than the income of a minimum-wage worker.

Yehiel Leiter, Israel's ambassador to the US, said that victory over the Islamic Republic means preventing Tehran from obtaining nuclear weapons and ending support for proxy forces. He accused the Islamic Republic of spreading an extremist form of Islam and stated that the regime's fall is necessary. Leiter also described US sanctions as a suffocating pressure on the regime.

Reza Shahbazi, deputy of geology at the Geological Survey Organization, stated that subsidence areas in Iran have expanded to about 100,000 square kilometers. Isfahan, Kerman, Tehran, Alborz, and Qazvin provinces are key subsidence regions. Subsidence has also spread towards the city center in Khorasan Razavi and Mashhad.

The Pentagon Inspector General reported to Congress that US forces conducted over 1,800 missions in Operation Epic Fury and targeted about 13,500 targets in Iran. The Pentagon also announced intercepting over 6,000 suicide drones and 1,500 ballistic missiles from the Islamic Republic. More details were provided by Amir Giti.

Siamak Javadi said that the intensification of US secondary sanctions makes banks and financial institutions worldwide more risk-averse in cooperating with Iran. Even banks not directly targeted by sanctions calculate the cost and risk of dealing with Iran. This limits the financial channels of the Islamic Republic and makes circumventing sanctions more costly.

Majid Mousavi, commander of the IRGC Aerospace Force, called for the continuation of supporters' presence in the regime's nightly gatherings. He described these gatherings as a "reliable support" for the armed forces. Mousavi also urged supporters to back the government and armed forces and to follow the Supreme Leader's guidance.

Shahram Khaledi said the US Department of War Inspector General's report shows that operations against the Islamic Republic continue in terms of budget and planning. The reduction in US ammunition reserves has increased the importance of boosting weapons production capacity. Washington is seeking to use non-military industries to strengthen its military production capabilities.

Hassan Qashqavi, spokesperson of the National Security Commission, stated that if freedom of navigation disrupts the coastal country's security, blockade is considered a form of war. He added that Iran's defense doctrine has changed in this war. The US insists only on freedom of navigation but does not respect Iran's national security and sovereignty.

Nicolas Gilani stated that increased US sanctions have pushed financial networks linked to the Islamic Republic towards smaller, riskier entities. He mentioned that with the sanction on Golden Global, Tehran is likely seeking alternatives in countries like Georgia and Malaysia. Additionally, the number of people willing to take the risk of cooperating with the Islamic Republic is decreasing.

Thamaneh Ghadarkhan, a journalist, says the most significant achievement of the Women, Life, Freedom movement is the change in social norms and the normalization of civil disobedience against mandatory hijab. She believes the Islamic Republic has failed to return society to its pre-1401 state. The perception of some parts of society about the possibility of political change has also shifted.

Mohsen Hakim, head of the VAR task force at the Football Federation, confirmed that incomplete VAR systems were used in some Premier League matches. The reason given was a budget shortage for purchasing the German VAR system license. He stated that from the new week of the Premier League, all matches will be held with the offside line.

September 15 is International Democracy Day, which this year the United Nations emphasizes the importance of hearing everyone's voice. According to Freedom House's latest assessment, only about one-fifth of the world's population lives in free countries. This report was prepared by Farzia Sabti from Iran International.

Pegah Bani-Hashemi stated that many detained protesters were denied access to their chosen lawyers. The trial process was not transparent and did not comply with fair trial principles. Additionally, individuals under 18 at the time of the crime should not face the death penalty.

Mohammad Qaedi says Saudi Arabia is under military and energy pressures and seeks help from Britain. The likelihood of British military involvement is low. London may increase its intelligence and defense cooperation with Saudi Arabia.

Hamidreza Hadadi was transferred to Shandiz clinic on January 8 after being shot by Khamenei's agents and died there. His name remains in the memory of this land. His memory is a guiding light for freedom seekers.

Jerusalem Post reported that Saudi Arabia has turned to Israel for intelligence assistance due to the rapid advance of Houthi forces in the Bab al-Mandeb Strait. Talks mediated by the US Central Command have taken place to support Saudi Arabia. Concerns have risen about security threats and restricted ship traffic in the region.

A citizen reacted to the closure of the Instagram page of the restaurant "Dastpokht Bibi" due to advertising Kotlet by sending a video. He introduced himself as Bibi and said he has Kotlet for dinner. Kotlet is a nickname used after Qasem Soleimani's death, and Bibi is the nickname of Benjamin Netanyahu.

Sohrab Bakhtiarizadeh praised his players and fans after Esteghlal's 3-0 victory over Al Sadd Qatar in the Asian Elite League. He expressed hope that the team will continue its successful run. He also explained the choice of Basra as the host city.

Mohammad Jafar Asadi stated that the region must be cleansed of the enemies of Islam and that the leaders of the countries should not allow the establishment of bases for the Great Satan. He said the people of the region will not permit such actions and that many defense surprises will be unveiled. Additionally, a significant part of the country's defense capability is carried by young Basij members.

People have reported economic difficulties and high medical and drug costs in Iran. Salaries do not cover living expenses, and the livelihood situation is especially critical for retirees and truck drivers. Additionally, the costs of national housing and education are reported to be very high.

The identity of Sarina Zaeri, one of the detained Baha'i citizens in Shiraz, has been confirmed. These individuals were arrested yesterday by security forces and transferred to an unknown location. Her family is concerned about her condition as she suffers from a respiratory illness.

Fatemeh Mohajerani stated that the government hopes there will be no need to change the first and second gasoline quotas. The adjustment of the third gasoline rate was postponed due to wartime conditions. If there are any changes in quotas or prices, the government will consult the public beforehand.

Yaser Asani, the Albanian player of Esteghlal, played a key role in his team's 3-0 victory against Al Sadd Qatar. He scored the first goal and assisted the second. Asani has recorded 10 goals and 2 assists in 11 Asian competition matches.

One of the two rescued American F-15 pilots, whose jet crashed in Iran five months ago, revealed in an interview with CBS that the United States deployed 92 elite soldiers to Iran for the first time in 46 years. This occurred after a CIA deception operation thwarted the Revolutionary Guard.

Aria Kasayi, a graphic designer who was arrested by security forces in Tehran in July, was released on Monday, September 13. The news was reported by HRANA news agency. Kasayi was arrested on July 19.

The Lebanese Minister of Interior met with the Pakistani army commander during an official visit to Pakistan. They discussed regional security developments and strengthening bilateral cooperation. The Pakistani army stated that both sides emphasized expanding security relations between the two countries.

Ahmad Alavi stated that the sanction on Russia's VTB Bank due to cooperation with the Islamic Republic could limit the shadow banking network activities related to both countries. This sanction makes the transfer of frozen funds and reserves more difficult. It also increases the risk and cost of banking transactions between Iran and Russia.

Mehdi Chamran, head of Tehran City Council, spoke about using metro stations as shelters during wartime. He emphasized that metro station infrastructure should be designed to serve as shelters. Previously, Mohsen Hashemi Rafsanjani stated that some officials used metro stations as workplaces during past wars.

Diplomatic sources report talks between Israel and Saudi Arabia mediated by the US Central Command. The talks aim to help Saudi Arabia counter Houthi attacks. This report is by Ashkan Safaei from Iran International.
The number of executions in Zahedan prison has increased to two. Another prisoner was executed early on Sunday, September 12. This report was published by Harana News Agency.

The father of Hamidreza Hemmati lit a candle at his son's grave by joining the campaign "One Candle, One Name, One Memory." Hamidreza Hemmati was a 21-year-old from Likak in Kohgiluyeh and Boyer-Ahmad. He was kidnapped in Isfahan on January 8, 2026, and after a few days, his lifeless body was returned to his family.

Alireza Beiranvand has requested a one-month delay in his military service enlistment. The medical commission session to review this request is scheduled for October 8. He intends to reduce his military service duration using childbearing service exemptions.

The Director General of the Mental Health Office of the Ministry of Health reported a shortage of certain specific psychiatric drugs. The supply of raw materials for these drugs depends on imports, and any disruption can worsen patients' symptoms. He emphasized the need for currency allocation and facilitation of imports to ensure a stable supply of psychiatric medications.

A video dated Tuesday, 24 Shahrivar, shows passengers at Tehran's Khomeini Airport angry due to a several-hour delay of the Tehran-Istanbul flight by Qeshm Air. This delay caused passenger dissatisfaction. The report was published by Iran International.

The US and Saudi Arabia plan to expand the southern shipping route through the Strait of Hormuz to counter the closure of the Bab al-Mandab Strait. This agreement was reached during a meeting between the CENTCOM commander and the Saudi crown prince. The US is also prepared to use military force against threats in the Strait of Hormuz.

The Islamic Republic has launched the 'Elaj' intelligence system to identify and collect information about Iranians abroad. This system allows reporting through a website, Telegram bot, and Bale messenger. This action may be reviewed in various countries including the UK, the US, and Canada.

The Austrian Foreign Ministry announced that Mohammad Eslami cannot attend the IAEA General Conference in Vienna due to UN sanctions and the rejection of an exemption request. This is because of his travel ban. More details were provided by Ahmad Samadi.

The head of the Wrestling Federation defended the exemption of the federation from obtaining technical and financial qualification certificates for entering the mining sector and considered it legal. The Supreme Mining Council unanimously granted this exemption to the Wrestling Federation. A member of parliament claimed the exemption was due to pressure on the Ministry of Industry and Mining.

Sajjad Babaafshari's sister joined the "One Candle, One Name, One Memory" campaign by lighting a candle at his grave. Sajjad Babaafshari was killed on January 8, 2026, in Hashtgerd. This act was done in his memory.

The head of the Emergency Organization announced that there are three thousand worn-out ambulances in the country, some of which have been in use for over 15 years. The optimal lifespan of ambulances is about 10 years, but due to current conditions, the worn-out fleet is still in use. Additionally, a shortage of personnel in cities like Isfahan, Tabriz, and Karaj is identified as a major challenge.

The UK Maritime Trade Operations received a delayed report of an incident in the Strait of Hormuz. A vessel was reportedly hit by an unidentified projectile. No damage or environmental impact has been reported so far.

Fadahossein Maleki proposed the formation of an Islamic NATO in opposition to Western NATO. He stated that this proposal has been accepted by many Islamic countries. Maleki emphasized that such an alliance is necessary to counter the crimes of Israel and the United States.

Workers of the Pey and Pol Jonoub company in Sirjan protested in front of the county governor's office. They are protesting unemployment and their job situation. The workers say the company is unable or unwilling to continue operations, and unemployment insurance will not cover their living expenses.

Naftali Bennett, former Prime Minister of Israel, described the Iranian government as decayed and said it will eventually collapse. He added that this government can be struck in various ways, not just military actions.

Olympic athletes have criticized Sydney Sweeney's new advertisement for a sports betting company. Sweeney appears semi-nude in the advertisement. The ad has faced strong reactions from female athletes.

Soran Feyzizadeh, 41 years old and father of two children, was severely injured in Bijar, Kurdistan province, due to baton blows and two pellets hitting his head, and died after a few days. His wife joined the campaign "One Candle, One Name, One Memory" and honored his memory.

Informed sources reported that body searches of female political prisoners in Evin Prison have intensified, including touching the body and forcing them to remove or pull aside clothing. These searches include touching breasts and violating human dignity. This practice has become routine in the women's ward in recent months.

The Instagram page of the restaurant Dastpokht Bibi was blocked by judicial order after posting a humorous story and the song "Bibi Gol" by Moein. The Saharkhizan restaurant in Rasht was closed after posting a humorous promotional video, and its manager was arrested on charges of insulting the hijab. These actions are part of ongoing government pressures on businesses.

A group of retirees from Zob Ahan and Foolad Isfahan held a protest in front of the Isfahan governor's office today. They demanded attention to their livelihood, health insurance issues, and the implementation of the adjustment plan. The protest took place on September 14.

Ali Shirazi stated that according to Article 30 of the Constitution, free education up to high school should be provided. He said the government has not fulfilled this duty. Additionally, public schools are charging fees from students' parents.

Ali Hossein Ghazizadeh suggested forming a global coalition with unified command to counter the Houthis. This coalition would coordinate land, air, and naval forces. The Houthis' advance in Bab al-Mandab and the threat to Red Sea security has made Western countries aware of the global costs of the crisis.

According to statistics from the Subsidy Targeting Organization, in August, 28,213,143 people were in the first to third income deciles. This number increased by more than 47,000 compared to July. Additionally, 73,437,712 people are in the first to ninth deciles and are eligible for cash subsidies.

Esmaeil Kowsari, a member of the National Security Commission of the Parliament, called for changes in the structure of the United Nations. He suggested that this should be done in cooperation with countries in the Shanghai Cooperation Organization and BRICS. He also emphasized the need to establish a new organization that treats all countries equally.

Four Kurdish political prisoners in Yazd and Evin prisons announced they will go on a hunger strike on Wednesday, September 25. They described the strike as the most civil form of protest and are joining the general strike on the anniversary of Mahsa Zhina Amini's death. The Coalition of Kurdish Political Forces in Iran also called for a general strike on the same day.

Morteza Kazemian said that the message from military and governmental institutions to continue pro-government gatherings indicates their concern about the re-emergence of street protests. He emphasized that government-organized gatherings are tools to intimidate and prevent protests. The legitimacy crisis and dissatisfaction with the Islamic Republic are deeper than what these measures can control.

Arash Azarmi, secretary of the economic section of Iran International, said that the US sanctions on Russian bank VTB limit one of the channels for the Islamic Republic to bypass sanctions and serve as a warning to other banks and financial institutions cooperating with it. He added that VTB's office in Tehran and the ruble-rial settlement mechanism have turned this bank into an important financial channel for Iran.

The oil tanker Algaya caught fire in the engine room following a drone attack by the IRGC and is being towed to a port in Oman. Twenty-three crew members have been evacuated, and two remain missing. The report was published by Reuters.

Hossein Abdi stated that Iran's U23 national team will face the UAE with only 15 players and three goalkeepers due to the match being outside the FIFA window and the absence of five players. Players from Esteghlal and Tractor will join the team on match day. Reza Ghandipour's absence is due to not being present during the FIFA window, and three forwards have been added as replacements.

Rasoul Sanaei-Rad, deputy for ideological-political affairs of Khamenei's office, described the rescue of two crew members of an F-15 downed in Iran as a media and propaganda ploy to cover American failures. He compared it to the film 'Saving Private Ryan' and said it aimed to boost soldier morale and influence the US domestic atmosphere ahead of upcoming elections.

The Iran Human Rights organization announced that at least 100 detainees from the December protests in 13 provinces of Iran face the death penalty. The highest number, 46 people, are from Isfahan province. This list includes those who have received death sentences at least at the preliminary stage.

Austria's Foreign Ministry announced that the request for a travel exemption for Mohammad Eslami, head of Iran's Atomic Energy Organization, to Vienna was rejected. The rejection was due to a lack of consensus in the UN Security Council. Eslami was not allowed to attend the International Atomic Energy Agency conference because of UN sanctions.

The US federal court on Monday, 23 Shahrivar, ruled against the implementation of the Trump administration's order to limit the stay duration of foreign students and journalists. The order, which the judge said had 'very weak arguments,' was set to be implemented on Tuesday. Under the law, foreign student visas would be limited to four years and journalist visas to 240 days.
Abdolrazagh Miraki and Mohammadans Allahdadzadeh were arrested by security forces in Saravan on August 17. Since their arrest, their whereabouts have been unknown. Their situation remains unclear.

The French club Lens has dismissed Dino Toppmöller after four weeks as head coach. He earned only 4 points in four Ligue 1 matches. The club management has temporarily assigned team leadership to Yannick Kawazek and Bilal Hamdi.

The security project 'Elaj' has published personal information of some Iranians abroad and asked citizens to identify and report more individuals. The Islamic Republic of Iran Broadcasting has also promoted this project. The responsible organization and the source of the published information are unknown.

Tehran police arrested a person who threw three Molotov cocktails at a crowd in Punak Square on the evening of Tuesday, September 14. The individual attempted to illegally cross the western borders and was injured in the right leg during the arrest. A similar incident occurred earlier on September 1 in Mashhad.

Sahand Nejatbakhsh, a chemical engineering undergraduate student at Iran University of Science and Technology, was sentenced to a one-semester suspension from studies. The disciplinary committee of the university issued this verdict. The ruling was made on September 14.

Farahnaz Salari, director of the Shamim Mehr Charity, stated that some beneficiaries sold their commodity baskets to buy school uniforms. She added that families cannot afford the items required for preschool children. These issues highlight the economic pressure on families to meet their children's educational needs.

Amir Raeisian announced that a criminal case has been filed against Reza Dormishian for propaganda against the regime. The case is being heard in Branch 7 of the Tehran Revolutionary Court. The Revolutionary Guard has requested the seizure of his assets as the plaintiff.
The Karageh studio announced that Aria Kasaei, a graphic designer and one of the founders of the studio, has been released after nearly two months of detention.

Hassan Qashqavi stated that the Islamic Republic offered an economic cooperation proposal worth about 500 billion dollars to American companies during three rounds of Geneva negotiations before the 12-day war. The proposal covered sectors including oil, gas, mining, environment, and transportation. The aim was to demonstrate economic opportunities and profitability of cooperation with Iran.

Behrouz Morvati announced that the subsidy for hygiene supplies for 13,000 people with severe and very severe disabilities has been cut by the Welfare Organization. He stated this action is unauthorized and warned that it could limit access to essential supplies for the disabled. Morvati also mentioned the price increase of hygiene items and the risks of using old supplies.

A Boeing 737 plane of Sepehran Airlines experienced a tire burst during its flight from Mashhad to Kermanshah on Tuesday, September 13. The plane had to return to Mashhad airport after reporting engine damage. A video showing the tense moments inside the plane has been released.

A special interview with Yechiel Leiter, Israel's ambassador to the US, will discuss Iran's regional influence and the role of proxy groups. Other topics include the impact of international sanctions, economic crisis, and rising regional tensions. The program will air tonight at 00:30 Tehran time.

Ali Tajernia, acting CEO of Esteghlal, spoke about the victory against Al Sadd and recent controversies. He criticized some fans for posting negative comments against other teams. Tajernia emphasized that such behavior is unpatriotic, and even Al Sadd had to close its comment section.

Sepideh Moafi was nominated for Best Supporting Actress at the 78th Primetime Emmy Awards for her role in the series "The Pitt." She is the first Iranian woman to be nominated in this category in Emmy history. The award went to Allison Janney.

The Houthi Foreign Ministry stated they have the full and legitimate right to target the gathering of Saudi forces. They also confirmed the safety of navigation in Bab al-Mandab and rejected Saudi Arabia's claims about the insecurity of this maritime route.

A person stated that due to the country's conditions, important life decisions such as having children and buying a house have been postponed. Long-term plans have been canceled, and only daily routines are followed. He believes that the country's situation has made controlling life difficult.

The US military destroyed two small Iranian boats after the IRGC attempted to seize a US Navy drone in the Strait of Hormuz. Most of the boat occupants were killed, and search and rescue operations are ongoing. The drone remains under US control.

Golareh Abbasi, a political activist and former political prisoner, announced that her account on Snapp was blocked. Snapp stated the reason for blocking was lack of necessary qualifications for cooperation. Abbasi attributed this action to Snapp's fear.

Ali Falih Al-Zaydi, the Prime Minister of Iraq, met with Friedrich Merz, the Chancellor of Germany, in Berlin on Tuesday, 24 Shahrivar, during his European trip. Al-Zaydi was welcomed at the Chancellor's office. This report was provided by Ahmad Samadi from Iran International.

A person in Iran stated that due to unfavorable economic and political conditions, many important life decisions such as continuing education, changing cars, marriage, and having children have been postponed. He complained about the lack of medical equipment and severe inflation, saying his life is almost halted. Additionally, the news of his wife's pregnancy caused him concern.

Saudi Arabia and Israel are in contact through CENTCOM, and Riyadh has requested intelligence assistance from Israel to counter Houthi attacks. Mohammed bin Salman has asked regional countries for help against the Houthis. The request for help from Israel was made indirectly through the United States.

Tensions between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis supported by the Islamic Republic continue. The Saudi Crown Prince arrived in Cairo to meet with the President of Egypt. Iran International reporters discussed reactions to the Houthis' threats and missile attacks.

Iran International has increased the display of names and images of more victims of the December protests with a new design. Families and relatives can submit information about the missing victims. More details are provided in an interview with Farnoush Faraji.

The mother of Ramin Hossein Panahi supported the call for a general strike in Kurdistan. This occurred on the eve of the fourth anniversary of Mahsa Amini's government killing. Additionally, the Association of Families of Ukrainian Plane Victims issued a statement supporting the "Woman, Life, Freedom" uprising.

Today, on 24 Shahrivar, applicants of the National Housing in Kashan held a protest in front of the county governor's office. They demand attention to their requests. They claim that despite paying the required amounts, the housing units have not been delivered to them.

A building under construction on Haft Tir Boulevard in Mashhad caught fire. The spokesperson for Mashhad Fire Department said 14 fire trucks from several stations are at the scene. Firefighting operations are ongoing.

Four Iranian football players, including Alireza Jahanbakhsh, Mehdi Qaedi, Ali Gholizadeh, and Majid Hosseini, have become subject to military service after their previous exemptions expired. They must take necessary actions to resolve their military service status. If they return to Iranian football, they may join military teams.

Scott Bessent, the US Treasury Secretary, said in Congress that they have seen positive remarks from the UAE about cutting off Iran's financial resources. He also reported good private talks with China about Iran's financial connections and added that these talks will continue with China's vice premier. Trump and Xi Jinping will also discuss Tehran later this month.

Ehsan Khandozi was appointed as the new head of the economic group of the Supreme Leader's office. His introduction ceremony was held on Tuesday morning, September 13. Khandozi was previously a representative of Tehran in the 11th parliament and served as the Minister of Economy in Ebrahim Raisi's government.

On Monday, 23 Shahrivar, the Intelligence Corps agents searched Raha Jalilian's home and confiscated some digital devices belonging to her family. Raha Jalilian was simultaneously summoned to the Intelligence Corps. The agents were unable to arrest her due to her absence.

The public running event in Kerman province was canceled following protests from the seminary about men and women running together. The cancellation was made under pressure from government institutions. An interview was conducted with Mehdi Rostampour, a sports journalist.

Mohammadjavad Fardous Khabazi and Amir Mohammad Ostaddoost were shot and killed on January 8, 2026, in Ramsar. Mohammadjavad Fardous Khabazi's mother lit a candle in their memory. This incident took place in Ramsar.

An Italian recreational ship will serve as a floating home for thousands of athletes and officials at the Nagoya Asian Games. This measure is due to the absence of a dedicated athletes' village. It is a different approach to hosting Asia's largest sporting event.

Ahead of the 2026 Asian Games in Japan, Nagoya port will host a luxury cruise ship that will serve as accommodation for athletes. The ship will be used as the floating village for the games from September 14 to October 6. This report was prepared by Somayeh Mehri.

Sirvan Habibi, a citizen from Sanandaj, was arrested on Wednesday, September 8, by intelligence officers in Kamyaran and transferred to an unknown location. About a week later, his family remains unaware of his status and whereabouts. This has increased the concern of his family and close ones.

Iraq's Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi stated that Iraq's oil sales have been severely affected by the situation in the Strait of Hormuz. He also mentioned that the crisis between the Islamic Republic and the United States has impacted the entire world. The German Chancellor said the coalition government will explore ways to help consumers cope with rising fuel prices.

Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, the Speaker of the Parliament, said that the United States never expected to be defeated by the Islamic Republic. He added that during the 40-day war, the US intended to take security action against Tehran from the Kurdistan region of Iraq, but this plot failed. Ghalibaf also emphasized that the US and Israel seek to create discord between Iran and Iraq.

The Houthis once again attacked the strategic pipeline of Saudi Arabia, and the Israeli newspaper Israel Hayom reported the formation of a US-led military coalition in support of Riyadh. Meanwhile, Mohammed bin Salman, in a message to the Egyptian president, said he will not surrender to the blackmail of the IRGC and Houthis in the straits.

Gol Gohar Sirjan drew 0-0 against Al Jazira UAE in their first AFC Champions League match. The game was held at Hissar Stadium in Dushanbe, Tajikistan, and Gol Gohar earned the club's first Asian points. Due to a hosting ban, Gol Gohar plays its home matches in Tajikistan.

Moshe Edri, head of Israel's Atomic Energy Commission, claimed that over 9 tons of nuclear material in Iran are outside the supervision of the International Atomic Energy Agency. This amount is equivalent to the material needed to build more than 10 nuclear bombs. He also referred to the Iranian regime's threat to destroy Israel.

One night before the fourth anniversary of Mahsa Zhina Amini's death, reports have emerged about the return of the morality police and plainclothes forces. People are reporting on the state of the streets and the city's lockdown. A program is being held to hear people's accounts of the streets in Iran.

The European Parliament reviewed a report on foreign interference and hybrid threats against member countries. Iran, along with Russia, China, Belarus, and North Korea, was named as a threat in the report. The President of the European Parliament called for the release of two imprisoned sisters in Iran.

Britain, the US, and the Netherlands issued a warning about the CHOSEN BRICK spyware used by agents linked to the Islamic Republic to target opponents and journalists. The spyware can steal emails, messages, and access microphones and social media accounts. The FBI stated that the Ministry of Intelligence of the Islamic Republic uses this spyware to collect information and harm individuals.

Asieh Ramazani, a mother of two, was killed by direct gunfire from the Islamic Republic forces during the protests on January 9, 2026, in Tehran. Her daughter lit a candle in memory of her mother and all victims of the Zhina Mahsa Amini uprising. This event was shared on social media.

The interrogation session of Mohammad Parsa Golchin, a University of Tehran student, was held at Mashhad Prosecutor's Office. He faces charges including conspiracy against internal security and propaganda against the regime. His bail was increased from two billion to fifteen billion tomans, and he was released after posting bail.

The head of Hamadan University of Medical Sciences reported a shortage of 800 nurses in the province. He also confirmed a shortage of assistant nurses and service staff. The recruitment limitation due to clause 'A' of Article 106 of the Seventh Development Plan has exacerbated this shortage.

Arjin Jandi, a 16-year-old child from the village of Kuper in Piranshahr, was arrested by security forces and subjected to torture for forced confession. The intelligence forces entered his home without a judicial warrant and arrested him. His family has had no information about his whereabouts for four days, and their inquiries have been unsuccessful.

Senior military commanders from the US, Israel, and several Arab countries held a secret meeting in Germany last week to discuss war with the Islamic Republic and regional tensions. The meeting was initiated by Brad Cooper, commander of CENTCOM. The agenda included plans to increase ship traffic in the Strait of Hormuz and Israeli military operations.

A citizen sent a video to Iran International on the anniversary of Zhina Mahsa Amini, holding the blood-stained flag of the Islamic Republic in protest against the killing of the unnamed martyrs. He said the regime's flag is stained with the blood of brave and innocent people. The citizen emphasized that they will not allow escape from this bloodshed.

Flora Samadani and Ahmad Naeimi, a Baháʼí couple residing in Yazd, have been summoned to the Revolutionary Court of Yazd. They are accused of educational or promotional activities contrary to Islamic law. The court session will be held on Tuesday, 31 Shahrivar 1405.

Nima Akbarpour stated that internet instability and outages have led more users to adopt Starlink. He also mentioned that filtering has imposed significant financial costs on people. Using anonymous VPNs has put users' personal information at risk.

Masoud Jafari, deputy coordinator of the Air Force, said Qatar has not provided clear information about the status of three Iranian pilots in Operation Al-Adid. He added that the Islamic Republic considers the pilots alive and captive until their fate is clarified. The Qatari government must be held accountable.

The prosecutor of Bijar announced the blocking of several active social media pages due to the publication of content against public decency and promoting unveiled behavior. Legal cases have been filed against the administrators of these pages. Four individuals have also been released on bail.

A video showing the birthday ceremony of Farid Ramazani at his grave has been released. Farid Ramazani was shot and killed on January 8 in the Aryashahr neighborhood of Tehran. Security forces targeted his right hand finger and fired a third bullet to his forehead.

Al Ain football team defeated Al Nassr Saudi Arabia 4-0 in the first week of the Asian Elite League. Al Ain's goals were scored by Hossein Rahimi (twice), Sofian Rahimi, and Giakoumakis. Al Nassr lost despite having Cristiano Ronaldo in their lineup.

Eyal Zamir, Chief of Staff of the Israeli army, described Hamas as defeated and said the group is currently not firing or responding. The Israeli army controls over 64% of the Gaza Strip. However, it has been warned that Hamas is trying to rebuild its military strength and recruit new forces.

The execution of two prisoners was carried out in the prisons of Dastgerd Isfahan and Ilam. These prisoners were sentenced to death for drug-related crimes and murder. Additionally, a prisoner sentenced to death in Anbarabad was spared from execution due to the victim's family's forgiveness.

The death sentence of Ali Rahimi Rigi, a detainee from the December protests, has been confirmed by the appeals court. He is accused of charges including waging war against God and corruption on earth. Ali Rigi accepted responsibility for the charges from the beginning and defended himself personally.

The United States has confirmed the attack on two Iranian boats and their destruction. This news was published in the audio version of Titrawol with Niusha Saremi. More details are provided in this report.

Mehdi Mahdavi Azad stated in the program "Cheshmandaz" that poverty alone is not the cause of protests; injustice, economic gaps, lack of future, and lack of motivation also lead to protests. He added that the Iranian government faces financial incapacity, internal conflicts, and loss of legitimacy.

Workers at the Tazareh coal mine in Damghan and Gilrad company in Rasht reported unpaid wages and insurance dues. Additionally, insurance for some construction workers in West Azerbaijan has been cut off. A labor activist criticized the consequences of this issue.

Today, several protests were held including housing applicants in Kashan and retirees in Isfahan. Yesterday, protests occurred among workers in Sirjan, Ahvaz, and job seekers in Shush. These protests were organized to demand attention to their issues.

Yahya Sari, the spokesperson for the Houthis, stated that Saudi warplanes conducted 52 airstrikes in the past 24 hours on the provinces of Taiz, Al-Jawf, Al-Bayda, Saada, and Amran. The Houthi Foreign Ministry declared the right to target Saudi forces' gatherings as legitimate. It also stated that navigation in Bab al-Mandab is safe and rejected Saudi claims about the insecurity of this maritime route.

Mohammad Akraminia, the army spokesperson, said that the US has become a nervous actor in its decline and cannot maintain its hegemony. He added that the recent war showed that the US priority is to protect its own and Israel's interests, not the security of regional countries. Therefore, imported security will never guarantee lasting peace.

Hossein Taeb, head of the Basij Organization, spoke about some countries' attempts to escort ships through the Strait of Hormuz with warships and air support. He said Iran's resistance did not allow these actions to succeed easily. These statements reflect Iran's stance in the region.
A viewer criticized the high food prices in a video sent to Iran International. He said people do not go to the streets out of fear of death. He described the living conditions as worse than death.

Britain, the US, and the Netherlands have warned about the spyware "Chosen Break" linked to the Islamic Republic, used to target opponents, activists, and journalists. This malware can steal emails and messages and access social networks, microphones, and device screens. Research, military, and technology institutions have also been targeted.

Farzin Karbasi, a political analyst, said that the continued closure of some Iran-Iraq borders is several times more damaging to Iran's economy than to Iraq's, and Baghdad is not willing to face US economic pressure for a few hundred million dollars in trade. He added that the Iraqi government controls the borders to assert its national sovereignty, although it does not have much control over the Islamic Republic's proxy forces.

The US Central Command, CENTCOM, announced that the destroyer USS Rafael Peralta is enforcing the US maritime blockade against Iran in the Arabian Sea. According to CENTCOM, US forces have rerouted 103 commercial vessels as of Tuesday to ensure compliance with the blockade.

Iranians in the UK commemorated the fourth anniversary of the 'Woman, Life, Freedom' movement on Tuesday. They remembered Mahsa Amini and the victims of the 1401 protests. The ceremony also honored the martyrs of the national revolution in 1404.

Masoud Pezeshkian requested mechanisms to facilitate and accelerate the renovation of the naval fleet damaged during the Iran war in the Supreme Council of Marine Industries meeting. He also proposed using the capacity of the Organization of Government Property to support the reconstruction of damaged ships. He emphasized that these supports should be managed so that all eligible parties can benefit from them.

A viewer of Iran International criticized the high prices of food items and the small size of potatoes in a video. He asked whether government officials themselves could use such small potatoes. The video highlights the market situation and product quality.

Abbas Araghchi, Iran's Foreign Minister, shared part of a Pentagon report stating that the idea of Iran being defenseless is incorrect. He said hundreds of buildings and military facilities in the US have been damaged or destroyed, and dozens of aircraft have been lost. Araghchi added that more details will be revealed at the appropriate time.

Reuters reported, citing calculations by the US Congressional Budget Office, that Iran's six-month war has so far cost the United States $38 billion, and this figure will increase by about $3 billion per month. According to the report, the costs are calculated through August 1, and the war is expected to increase US inflation by 0.5 percent in the first quarter of 2027.
Liverpool defeated Tottenham 3-1 in the English Football League Cup. Liverpool's goals were scored by McAllister, Akpom, and Szoboszlai. Tottenham scored for the first time this season.

Real Madrid defeated Elche 3-2 in the sixth week of La Liga. The goals for Real Madrid were scored by Matias Dituro (own goal), Kylian Mbappe, and Carlos Aspe. Elche equalized in the second half, but the winning goal was scored by Carlos Aspe.

The Iran Human Rights Campaign reported the death sentence for Hossein Rasouli-Nasab. This sentence concerns detainees from the December 2025 protests. Concerns about the lives of other detainees have increased due to security charges.

The French representative at the Security Council meeting called on the Islamic Republic to stop arming the Houthis and violating the arms embargo. He also urged the Houthis to cease all military actions immediately. The French representative expressed solidarity with the legitimate government of Yemen and Saudi Arabia.

On the anniversary of Mahsa's government killing, suppression forces have returned to the streets. This issue was discussed in a program with Kambiz Hosseini. The audio version of this program has been released.

Hanna Neumann, a Green Party representative in the European Parliament, wrote about the Iranian regime's repression following the death of Zhina Mahsa Amini. She emphasized that the new generation has changed Iran, but the regime remains unchanged. Neumann stated she will work to ensure the European Union continues to support the Women, Life, Freedom movement.

A project called 'Elaj' asks people to report those it calls traitors and send their personal information. This includes collecting names, addresses, jobs, family members' information, and social media accounts. Kambiz Hosseini discusses this topic in a program.

Mozhgan Eftekhari, the mother of Mahsa Zhina Amini, released a message with Mahsa's voice on the eve of the fourth anniversary of her daughter's death. She wrote that Zhina means death is not the end of life. She also emphasized that Mahsa symbolizes the importance of women and girls in society.

Pouria Bakhtiari stated that due to Ebrahim Raisi's misunderstanding of economic concepts, a team created short animations to teach him. Raisi's foundation denied this claim and filed a complaint against Bakhtiari. This issue was discussed in a program hosted by Kambiz Hosseini.

Thomas Massey, a Republican member of the US Congress, has introduced an eight-point resolution to impeach Pete Hegseth, the US Secretary of War. Massey accuses Hegseth of illegally continuing the war with the Islamic Republic and defying Congress. This report was published by Marzieh Hosseini from Iran International.

The Washington Post reported that the Trump administration is preparing a $2.8 billion weapons package for Israel. This package includes 20,000 MK-84 bombs, 20,000 BLU-117 bombs, and 20,000 I-2000 penetrator warheads.
